TextOut@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes a character string at the specified x,y location using the currently selected font, background color and text color. Returns nonzero on success.

ExtTextOut@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws text using the current font, with optional clipping/opaquing rectangle and an optional array of character spacing values. Returns nonzero on success.

PolyTextOut@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws several strings in one call, each described by a POLYTEXT structure, using the font and text colors selected into the device context.

CreatePolygonRgn@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a polygonal region from an array of points; the fill mode (ALTERNATE or WINDING) decides which areas are inside. Returns the region handle or 0.

DPtoLP@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts an array of points from device coordinates to logical coordinates, using the device context's current mapping mode and transformations.

LPtoDP@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts an array of points from logical coordinates to device coordinates, using the device context's current mapping mode and transformations.

Polyline@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws a series of connected line segments through the given array of points with the current pen. Does not use or update the current position.

Polygon@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws a closed polygon through the given points, outlined with the current pen and filled with the current brush using the polygon fill mode.

PolyBezier@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws one or more cubic Bezier curves from an array of endpoints and control points (count must be 3n+1). Does not use or update the current position.

PolyBezierTo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws cubic Bezier curves starting at the current position, using points in groups of three; updates the current position to the last endpoint.

PolylineTo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Draws connected lines from the current position through the given points and sets the current position to the last point.

SetViewportExtEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the horizontal and vertical viewport extents (device units) of a device context; used with MM_ISOTROPIC/MM_ANISOTROPIC. Can return the previous extents.

SetViewportOrgEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets which device point maps to the window origin (the viewport origin) of a device context. Can return the previous origin.

SetWindowOrgEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets which logical point maps to the viewport origin (the window origin) of a device context. Can return the previous origin.

SetWindowExtEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the horizontal and vertical window extents (logical units) of a device context; used with MM_ISOTROPIC/MM_ANISOTROPIC. Can return the previous extents.

OffsetViewportOrgEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Moves the viewport origin of a device context by the given horizontal and vertical offsets (device units).

OffsetWindowOrgEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Moves the window origin of a device context by the given horizontal and vertical offsets (logical units).

ScaleWindowExtEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Scales the window extents of a device context by the ratios formed from the given multiplicands and divisors.

ScaleViewportExtEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Scales the viewport extents of a device context by the ratios formed from the given multiplicands and divisors.

SetBitmapDimensionEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Assigns preferred dimensions to a bitmap, in 0.1 mm units, for use by applications; GDI itself does not use them.

SetBrushOrgEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the brush origin that GDI assigns to the next brush selected into the device context. Can return the previous origin.

GetTextFace@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies the typeface name of the font selected into a device context into a buffer. Returns the number of characters copied, or 0 on failure.

GetKerningPairs@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the kerning pairs of the font selected into a device context into an array of KERNINGPAIR structures. Returns the number of pairs.

GetDCOrgEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the final translation origin of a device context, i.e. the offset GDI uses to convert device coordinates to client/screen coordinates.

UnrealizeObject@WIN32API.INC.desc: Resets the origin of a brush or resets a logical palette so it is remapped when next realized. Brush origin use is obsolete on Win32 (use SetBrushOrgEx).

GdiFlush@WIN32API.INC.desc: Flushes the calling thread's current batch of pending GDI drawing calls. Returns nonzero if all calls in the batch succeeded.

GdiSetBatchLimit@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the maximum number of GDI calls that can be batched for the calling thread before they are flushed. Returns the previous limit; mostly a no-op on modern Windows.

GdiGetBatchLimit@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the maximum number of GDI function calls that can be batched for the calling thread.

EnumFontFamilies@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the fonts in a font family (or one font of each family if no name is given), calling a callback for each. Superseded by EnumFontFamiliesEx.

EnumFontFamiliesEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates all fonts on a device matching the face name and character set in a LOGFONT, calling a callback function for each font found.

GetTextCharset@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the character set identifier (e.g. ANSI_CHARSET) of the font currently selected into a device context, or DEFAULT_CHARSET on failure.

GetTextCharsetInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the character set of the font selected into a device context and optionally fills a FONTSIGNATURE structure with its Unicode and code page coverage.

TranslateCharsetInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates between a character set, code page or font signature value and fills a CHARSETINFO structure with the corresponding values.

GetFontLanguageInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns flags describing the font currently selected into a device context, such as whether it needs reordering, glyph shaping or has diacritics.

GetCharacterPlacement@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about a string (character widths, caret positions, ordering, glyphs) needed for layout and display. Largely superseded by Uniscribe. The ALIAS in WIN32API.INC was wrong; the build uses "GetCharacterPlacementA".

SetICMMode@WIN32API.INC.desc: Turns Image Color Management (ICM) on, off or queries its state for a device context. Returns the previous or current mode.

CheckColorsInGamut@WIN32API.INC.desc: Checks whether each color in an array of RGB triples lies within the output gamut of the device context, filling a result buffer.

GetLogColorSpace@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the LOGCOLORSPACE structure that describes the given logical color space handle.

GetColorSpace@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a handle to the logical color space currently selected into a device context.

CreateColorSpace@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates a logical color space from a LOGCOLORSPACE structure. Returns the color space handle, or 0 on failure.

SetColorSpace@WIN32API.INC.desc: Selects a logical color space into a device context. Returns the handle of the previously selected color space.

DeleteColorSpace@WIN32API.INC.desc: Deletes a logical color space and frees its system resources. Returns nonzero on success.

GetICMProfile@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the file name of the current output color profile for a device context. The buffer size parameter receives the required length.

SetICMProfile@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the specified color profile file as the output profile for a device context. Returns nonzero on success.

GetDeviceGammaRamp@WIN32API.INC.desc: Gets the gamma ramp of a display device (three arrays of 256 WORD values for red, green and blue).

SetDeviceGammaRamp@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the gamma ramp of a display device that supports gamma ramps (three arrays of 256 WORD values for red, green and blue).

ColorMatchToTarget@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enables or disables preview of a target device's colors (e.g. a printer) on a display device context using ICM.

EnumICMProfiles@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the color profile files supported by a device context, calling an application callback for each profile.

LoadKeyboardLayout@WIN32API.INC.desc: Loads a keyboard layout given its identifier string (e.g. "00000409") and optionally activates it. Returns the input locale handle (HKL) or 0.

ActivateKeyboardLayout@WIN32API.INC.desc: Activates a loaded input locale (HKL) for the calling thread or process. Returns the previous input locale handle, or 0 on failure.

UnloadKeyboardLayout@WIN32API.INC.desc: Unloads an input locale identifier (HKL) previously loaded with LoadKeyboardLayout. Returns nonzero on success.

GetKeyboardLayoutName@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the name (KLID string, e.g. "00000409") of the active keyboard layout for the calling thread into a buffer of at least 9 characters.

GetThreadDesktop@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a handle to the desktop assigned to the specified thread, or 0 on failure.

SetUserObjectSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the security descriptor of a user object such as a window station or desktop.

GetUserObjectSecurity@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves security information (a security descriptor) for a user object such as a window station or desktop.

RegisterWindowMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Defines a new window message number that is unique system-wide for the given string. Returns the message identifier (0xC000-0xFFFF), or 0 on failure.

GetMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a message from the calling thread's message queue, waiting if none is available. Returns 0 for WM_QUIT, -1 on error, otherwise nonzero.

TranslateMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates virtual-key messages into character messages (WM_CHAR etc.) and posts them to the thread's message queue.

DispatchMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Dispatches a message retrieved by GetMessage or PeekMessage to the window procedure of its target window. Returns the window procedure's result.

PeekMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Checks the thread's message queue for a message without waiting and optionally removes it (PM_REMOVE). Returns nonzero if a message is available.

ExitWindows@WIN32API.INC.desc: Logs off the interactive user. Microsoft documents it as a macro that calls ExitWindowsEx(EWX_LOGOFF, ...); user32 normally exports only ExitWindowsEx.

SwapMouseButton@WIN32API.INC.desc: Reverses (TRUE) or restores (FALSE) the meaning of the left and right mouse buttons. Returns nonzero if the buttons were swapped before the call.

SendMessageTimeout@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sends a message to a window and waits for it to be processed, but returns after the given timeout or if the receiving thread is hung.

SendNotifyMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sends a message to a window; waits for processing if the window belongs to the calling thread, otherwise returns immediately.

SendMessageCallback@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sends a message to a window and returns immediately; the system calls the given callback function when the window procedure has processed it.

PostThreadMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Posts a message to the message queue of the specified thread and returns without waiting. Returns nonzero on success.

AttachThreadInput@WIN32API.INC.desc: Attaches or detaches the input processing (focus, active window, key state) of one thread to that of another thread.

ReplyMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Replies to a message sent by another thread via SendMessage, so the sender can continue while the receiver keeps processing.

WaitMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Yields control and suspends the thread until a new message is placed in its message queue.

WaitForInputIdle@WIN32API.INC.desc: Waits until the specified process has finished initialization and is waiting for user input, or until the timeout elapses. Returns 0 on success.

PostQuitMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Posts WM_QUIT with the given exit code to the thread's message queue, telling the message loop to end.

InSendMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns nonzero if the current window procedure is processing a message sent from another thread with SendMessage.

SetDoubleClickTime@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the maximum time in milliseconds between two clicks that counts as a double-click. Zero restores the default of 500 ms.

RegisterClass@WIN32API.INC.desc: Registers a window class (WNDCLASS) for use with CreateWindow/CreateWindowEx. Returns a class atom, or 0 on failure. The ALIAS in WIN32API.INC was wrong; the build uses "RegisterClassA".

UnregisterClass@WIN32API.INC.desc: Unregisters a window class and frees its memory. All windows of the class must be destroyed first. Returns nonzero on success.

GetClassInfo@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves information about a window class into a WNDCLASS structure. Returns nonzero if the class was found.

CreateWindowEx_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates an overlapped, pop-up or child window with an extended style, given class name, title, style, position, size, parent and menu. Returns the window handle or 0.

IsWindow@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether the given handle identifies an existing window. Returns nonzero if it does.

IsMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a handle is a menu handle. Returns nonzero if it is.

IsChild@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a window is a child or descendant of the specified parent window. Returns nonzero if it is.

DestroyWindow@WIN32API.INC.desc: Destroys the specified window, sending WM_DESTROY and WM_NCDESTROY and destroying its child windows. Returns nonzero on success.

FlashWindow@WIN32API.INC.desc: Flashes the specified window's title bar and taskbar button once (bInvert TRUE) or restores it. See also FlashWindowEx.

ShowOwnedPopups@WIN32API.INC.desc: Shows or hides all pop-up windows owned by the specified window.

OpenIcon@WIN32API.INC.desc: Restores a minimized (iconic) window to its previous size and position and activates it.

CloseWindow@WIN32API.INC.desc: Minimizes (does not destroy) the specified window. Returns nonzero on success.

GetWindowPlacement_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the show state and the restored, minimized and maximized positions of a window into a WINDOWPLACEMENT structure (set its length field first).

SetWindowPlacement_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the show state and the restored, minimized and maximized positions of a window from a WINDOWPLACEMENT structure.

BeginDeferWindowPos@WIN32API.INC.desc: Allocates a multiple-window-position structure for the given number of windows. Returns a handle to pass to DeferWindowPos and EndDeferWindowPos.

DeferWindowPos@WIN32API.INC.desc: Adds a window's new position, size and z-order to a multiple-window-position structure. Returns the (possibly updated) handle to use next.

EndDeferWindowPos@WIN32API.INC.desc: Moves and sizes all windows recorded in a multiple-window-position structure in a single screen refresh.

EndDialog@WIN32API.INC.desc: Destroys a modal dialog box, ending its processing; the given result value is returned by the DialogBox call that created it.

GetDlgItem@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the window handle of the control with the given identifier in a dialog box, or 0 if not found.

SetDlgItemInt@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the text of a dialog box control to the string form of an integer (signed or unsigned).

GetDlgItemInt@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates the text of a dialog box control into an integer; an optional flag receives success or failure.

SetDlgItemText@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the title or text of a control in a dialog box. Returns nonzero on success.

GetDlgItemText@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies the title or text of a dialog box control into a buffer. Returns the number of characters copied.

CheckDlgButton@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the check state of a check box or radio button in a dialog (BST_CHECKED, BST_UNCHECKED, BST_INDETERMINATE). The ALIAS in WIN32API.INC was wrong; the build uses "CheckDlgButton".

CheckRadioButton@WIN32API.INC.desc: Checks one radio button in a dialog and clears all others in the given ID range. The ALIAS in WIN32API.INC was wrong; the build uses "CheckRadioButton".

IsDlgButtonChecked@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the check state of a button control in a dialog: BST_CHECKED, BST_UNCHECKED or BST_INDETERMINATE.

SendDlgItemMessage@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sends a message to the control with the given identifier in a dialog box. Returns the result of the message processing.

GetNextDlgGroupItem@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the handle of the previous or next control in the same group as the given control in a dialog box.

GetNextDlgTabItem@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the handle of the previous or next control with the WS_TABSTOP style in a dialog box.

GetDlgCtrlID@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the identifier of the specified control (child window), or 0 on failure.

DefDlgProc@WIN32API.INC.desc: Provides default message processing for windows of a custom dialog class (window procedure of the dialog class).

CallMsgFilter@WIN32API.INC.desc: Passes a message and hook code to the WH_SYSMSGFILTER and WH_MSGFILTER hook procedures. Returns nonzero if a hook processed the message.

OpenClipboard@WIN32API.INC.desc: Opens the clipboard for examination and prevents other applications from changing it; the window becomes owner after EmptyClipboard. Returns nonzero on success.

CloseClipboard@WIN32API.INC.desc: Closes the clipboard so other windows can access it. Returns nonzero on success.

GetClipboardOwner@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the handle of the window that currently owns the clipboard, or 0.

SetClipboardViewer@WIN32API.INC.desc: Adds a window to the chain of clipboard viewers, which receive WM_DRAWCLIPBOARD. Returns the next window in the chain. Superseded by AddClipboardFormatListener.

GetClipboardViewer@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the handle of the first window in the clipboard viewer chain, or 0.

ChangeClipboardChain@WIN32API.INC.desc: Removes a window from the chain of clipboard viewers, given the window and the next window in the chain.

SetClipboardData@WIN32API.INC.desc: Places data (a global memory handle) on the clipboard in the given format; the clipboard must be open. The ALIAS in WIN32API.INC was wrong; the build uses "SetClipboardData".

GetClipboardData@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a handle to clipboard data in the given format (e.g. CF_TEXT); the clipboard must be open. The ALIAS in WIN32API.INC was wrong; the build uses "GetClipboardData".

RegisterClipboardFormat@WIN32API.INC.desc: Registers a new clipboard format name. Returns the format identifier (0xC000-0xFFFF); the same name always gets the same value.

CountClipboardFormats@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the number of different data formats currently on the clipboard.

EnumClipboardFormats@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enumerates the formats currently on the clipboard: pass 0 to get the first, then the previous value to get the next. Returns 0 when done.

GetClipboardFormatName@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies the name of a registered clipboard format into a buffer. Returns the length of the name, or 0 for predefined formats.

EmptyClipboard@WIN32API.INC.desc: Empties the clipboard, frees its data handles and gives ownership to the window that opened it. Returns nonzero on success.

IsClipboardFormatAvailable@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns nonzero if the clipboard contains data in the specified format.

GetPriorityClipboardFormat@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the first format from a priority list that is available on the clipboard; 0 if the clipboard is empty, -1 if none match.

CharToOemBuff@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates a given number of characters from the ANSI (or wide) character set to the OEM character set.

OemToCharBuff@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates a given number of characters from the OEM character set to the ANSI (or wide) character set.

CharUpperBuff@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a given number of characters in a buffer to uppercase in place. Returns the number of characters processed.

CharLowerBuff@WIN32API.INC.desc: Converts a given number of characters in a buffer to lowercase in place. Returns the number of characters processed.

CharNext@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a pointer to the next character in a string, handling multibyte characters.

CharPrev@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a pointer to the preceding character in a string, handling multibyte characters.

IsCharAlpha@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a character is alphabetic, based on the language selected by the user. Returns nonzero if it is.

IsCharAlphaNumeric@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a character is alphabetic or numeric, based on the user's language. Returns nonzero if it is.

IsCharUpper@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a character is uppercase, based on the user's language. Returns nonzero if it is.

IsCharLower@WIN32API.INC.desc: Determines whether a character is lowercase, based on the user's language. Returns nonzero if it is.

GetAsyncKeyState@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns whether a key is up or down at the time of the call: the high bit is set if the key is down. Takes a virtual-key code.

GetKeyboardState@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies the status of all 256 virtual keys into a 256-byte array (high bit = down, low bit = toggled). Returns nonzero on success.

SetKeyboardState@WIN32API.INC.desc: Replaces the calling thread's keyboard state table with the values in a 256-byte array of virtual-key states.

GetKeyboardType@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns information about the keyboard: its type (0), subtype (1) or number of function keys (2), depending on the parameter.

GetKeyNameText@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the name of a key (e.g. "Shift") from the lParam of a keyboard message. Returns the length of the name copied.

ToAscii@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates a virtual-key code and keyboard state to the corresponding character(s). Returns the number of characters produced (0, 1 or 2).

ToUnicode@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates a virtual-key code and keyboard state to the corresponding Unicode character(s). Returns the count, or -1 for a dead key.

OemKeyScan@WIN32API.INC.desc: Maps an OEM ASCII code (0-0FFh) to its OEM scan code and shift state.

VkKeyScan@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates a character to its virtual-key code (low byte) and the shift state needed (high byte) for the current keyboard layout.

keybd_event@WIN32API.INC.desc: Synthesizes a keystroke (key down or up for a virtual-key code). Superseded by SendInput.

MapVirtualKey@WIN32API.INC.desc: Translates between virtual-key codes, scan codes and character values, depending on the map type parameter.

GetQueueStatus@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the types of messages found in the calling thread's message queue (high word: currently in queue; low word: added since last check).

MsgWaitForMultipleObjects@WIN32API.INC.desc: Waits until one or all specified objects are signaled, the timeout elapses, or input of the given types arrives in the thread's queue.

KillTimer@WIN32API.INC.desc: Destroys a timer created by SetTimer for the given window and timer identifier. Returns nonzero on success.

IsWindowUnicode@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns nonzero if the specified window is a native Unicode window (its window procedure receives Unicode messages).

IsWindowEnabled@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns nonzero if the specified window is enabled for mouse and keyboard input.

LoadAccelerators@WIN32API.INC.desc: Loads an accelerator table resource from a module. Returns the accelerator table handle, or 0 on failure.

CreateAcceleratorTable@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates an accelerator table from an array of ACCEL structures. Returns the table handle; free it with DestroyAcceleratorTable.

DestroyAcceleratorTable@WIN32API.INC.desc: Destroys an accelerator table created with CreateAcceleratorTable.

CopyAcceleratorTable@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies an accelerator table into an array of ACCEL structures, or returns the number of entries if the array is null.

TranslateAccelerator@WIN32API.INC.desc: Processes accelerator keys: translates a WM_KEYDOWN/WM_SYSKEYDOWN into WM_COMMAND using the table and sends it to the window. Returns nonzero if translated.

LoadMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Loads a menu resource from a module. Returns the menu handle, or 0 on failure.

LoadMenuIndirect@WIN32API.INC.desc: Loads a menu from a menu template in memory. Returns the menu handle, or 0 on failure.

SetMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Assigns a new menu to a window (0 removes the menu). Returns nonzero on success.

HiliteMenuItem@WIN32API.INC.desc: Highlights or removes the highlight from an item in a window's menu bar.

GetMenuString@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies the text string of a menu item into a buffer, identified by command ID or position. Returns the number of characters copied.

GetMenuState@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the menu flags (checked, grayed, etc.) of a menu item, or for a submenu the item count in the high byte. Returns -1 if the item does not exist.

DrawMenuBar@WIN32API.INC.desc: Redraws the menu bar of a window; call it after changing the menu bar.

GetSystemMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns a handle to the window menu (system menu) of a window for copying and modifying, or resets it to the default (bRevert TRUE).

CreateMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates an empty menu (menu bar). Returns the menu handle, or 0 on failure.

CreatePopupMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Creates an empty drop-down, submenu or shortcut menu. Returns the menu handle, or 0 on failure.

DestroyMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Destroys the specified menu and frees its memory, including submenus. Returns nonzero on success.

CheckMenuItem@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the check-mark state of a menu item (MF_CHECKED/MF_UNCHECKED). Returns the previous state, or -1 if the item does not exist.

EnableMenuItem@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enables, disables or grays a menu item (MF_ENABLED, MF_DISABLED, MF_GRAYED). Returns the previous state, or -1 if the item does not exist.

GetSubMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the handle of the drop-down menu or submenu at the given position in a menu, or 0.

GetMenuItemID@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the command identifier of the menu item at the given position, or -1 if it opens a submenu or does not exist.

GetMenuItemCount@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the number of items in a menu, or -1 on failure.

InsertMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Inserts a new menu item into a menu before the given item, moving other items down. Superseded by InsertMenuItem.

AppendMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Appends a new item (string, bitmap, separator or submenu) to the end of a menu. Returns nonzero on success.

RemoveMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Removes a menu item or detaches a submenu from a menu without destroying the submenu. Returns nonzero on success.

DeleteMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Deletes an item from a menu; if it opens a submenu, the submenu is destroyed too. Returns nonzero on success.

SetMenuItemBitmaps@WIN32API.INC.desc: Associates bitmaps to display next to a menu item instead of the default checked and unchecked marks.

TrackPopupMenu@WIN32API.INC.desc: Displays a shortcut menu at the given screen position and tracks the selection. Returns the chosen ID if TPM_RETURNCMD, otherwise nonzero on success.

TabbedTextOut@WIN32API.INC.desc: Writes a string at a location, expanding tabs to the given tab-stop positions. Returns the string's width and height packed in a long.

GetTabbedTextExtent@WIN32API.INC.desc: Computes the width (low word) and height (high word) of a string containing tabs, using the given tab stops and the current font.

UpdateWindow@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sends WM_PAINT directly to the window if its update region is not empty, so it is repainted immediately.

WindowFromDC@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the handle of the window associated with a display device context, or 0.

GetDCEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves a device context for the client area or entire window, with options controlling clipping. Release it with ReleaseDC.

BeginPaint@WIN32API.INC.desc: Prepares a window for painting, fills a PAINTSTRUCT and returns a display DC. Use only in response to WM_PAINT and pair with EndPaint.

EndPaint@WIN32API.INC.desc: Marks the end of painting in a window started with BeginPaint and releases its device context.

GetUpdateRect@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the smallest rectangle enclosing the window's update region. Returns nonzero if the update region is not empty.

GetUpdateRgn@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies a window's update region into an existing region handle. Returns the region type (e.g. NULLREGION, SIMPLEREGION).

RedrawWindow_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Updates a rectangle or region in a window's client area, with flags to invalidate, validate, erase or repaint immediately.

LockWindowUpdate@WIN32API.INC.desc: Disables (hwnd) or re-enables (0) drawing in the specified window; only one window can be locked at a time.

ScrollWindow@WIN32API.INC.desc: Scrolls the contents of a window's client area by the given amounts. Superseded by ScrollWindowEx.

ScrollDC@WIN32API.INC.desc: Scrolls a rectangle of bits in a device context horizontally and vertically, and can return the uncovered region.

ScrollWindowEx@WIN32API.INC.desc: Scrolls the contents of a window's client area, with options to scroll children, invalidate and erase the uncovered area.

SetScrollPos@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the position of the scroll box in a scroll bar and optionally redraws it. Returns the previous position. Superseded by SetScrollInfo.

GetScrollPos@WIN32API.INC.desc: Returns the current position of the scroll box in a window's scroll bar or scroll bar control. Superseded by GetScrollInfo.

SetScrollRange@WIN32API.INC.desc: Sets the minimum and maximum positions of a scroll bar. Superseded by SetScrollInfo.

GetScrollRange@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the minimum and maximum positions of a scroll bar. Superseded by GetScrollInfo.

ShowScrollBar@WIN32API.INC.desc: Shows or hides the specified scroll bar(s) of a window (SB_HORZ, SB_VERT, SB_BOTH, SB_CTL).

EnableScrollBar@WIN32API.INC.desc: Enables or disables one or both scroll bar arrows (ESB_ENABLE_BOTH, ESB_DISABLE_BOTH, etc.).

SetWindowText_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Changes the title bar text of a window, or the text of a control. Returns nonzero on success.

GetWindowText_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Copies the title bar text of a window, or the text of a control, into a buffer. Returns the length of the copied string.

GetClientRect_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the coordinates of a window's client area; left and top are 0, so right and bottom give the width and height.

GetWindowRect_WIN32API@WIN32API.INC.desc: Retrieves the bounding rectangle of a window, including borders and title bar, in screen coordinates.

AdjustWindowRect@WIN32API.INC.desc: Calculates the window rectangle needed for a desired client-area rectangle, given the window style and whether it has a menu.
